trust_decision.summary: SSRF: a caller-supplied url= is fetched with a bare requests.get that applies no scheme, hostname, port or resolved-address validation, so an attacker-chosen URL makes the library issue HTTP requests to loopback/link-local/internal addresses (cloud metadata); the decision is made (absent) at each individual call site, there is no shared choke point at the pinned commit.

landing_point.why: The summary says URL-based partitioning; partition(url=...) is the documented 'url for a remote document' public API (unstructured/partition/auto.py:73-74) and its fetch lives in file_and_type_from_url at auto.py:303-310, so that is the first place an engineer reads.

fix_sites.module_kind: markdown partitioner module (separate ad-hoc fetch implementation)

fix_sites.entry_point: none of its own; consumed by the three partitioners above (fix-added module unstructured/safe_http.py, absent at the pinned commit)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared library helper added at the top-level unstructured package

O3_reason_to_dismiss: partition_md is a neighbouring markdown feature with its own ad-hoc fetch and its own text/markdown content-type gate (md.py:101-105), so a solver can argue the advisory's URL-partitioning flaw is about the HTML/document path and that md was never named.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate per-request knobs on the same sink must keep working: partition_html(url=..., headers={...}, ssl_verify=False) for authenticated/self-signed hosts (partition.py:62-66) and partition(url=..., request_timeout=...) which must still be routed to the HTTP call (test_unstructured/partition/test_auto.py:1008-1020); an over-broad fix that blocks all URL fetching, or swaps in a helper that drops headers/verify/timeout, breaks documented usage. The published fix itself had to add an allow_private/UNSTRUCTURED_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URL opt-out (fix.diff:14) because private/intranet URLs are a real use case.

O6_input_shapes: IP literals and their abbreviated/decimal forms, including blocked ranges 127/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16, 0.0.0.0, 100.64/10, multicast/reserved (fix.diff:852-883)
IPv6 literals incl. bracketed forms, ::ffff: IPv4-mapped, 6to4 2002::/16, NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, IPv4-compatible ::/96 (fix.diff:863-869, 974-975)
hostname that resolves to a non-routable address (DNS-time check, fix.diff:945-954) and re-resolves to one at connect time (rebinding window, fix.diff:977-988)
non-http schemes: file, ftp, gopher, data, javascript (fix.diff:921-924)
explicit vs out-of-range port on the URL (fix.diff:915-919)
redirect chains: relative Location, cross-origin Location, >10 hops (fix.diff:1171-1186)
proxies= kwarg and HTTP(S)_PROXY env pickup, refused unless bypassed (fix.diff:1150-1155, 1162-1165)
IDNA/trailing-dot hostname forms for denylist comparison (fix.diff:886-898)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a url= branch in partition_rst/partition_org/partition_epub that fetches with its own requests.get, the way partition_md does
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: rst/org/epub are direct siblings of partition_md and already delegate to partition_html (rst.py:43, org.py:43, epub.py:54); md.py:96-107 shows maintainers wrote exactly this per-format ad-hoc fetch instead of a shared helper, so the same patch is plausible for a maintainer adding url support to another text format.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fetching remote /data-src URLs while parsing HTML so image blocks carry bytes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ImageBlock already records image_url without fetching (html/parser.py:515-522) and partition_html exposes extract_image_block_types/extract_image_block_to_payload (html/partition.py:41-42), so a maintainer adding remote-image support would requests.get an attacker-controlled src there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: partition_via_api/partition_multiple_via_api POSTing document bytes to a caller-supplied api_url
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: api_url is a plain public parameter (api.py:29), i.e. an outbound request whose destination the caller controls; the published fix left this untouched, so a maintainer hardening outbound requests later would plausibly extend the helper here.

O9_family: server-side request forgery (CWE-918), with CWE-601 open-redirect handling for per-hop redirect re-validation

O10_build.toolchain: hatchling build backend (pyproject.toml:150-152), uv dependency groups incl. a 'test' group with pytest/pytest-mock/pytest-xdist (pyproject.toml:163-182); md tests need the optional 'md' extra (markdown, pyproject.toml:75-77)
O10_build.project_tests: test_unstructured/partition/html/test_partition.py:111-250 and :1214-1223 cover the url path incl. headers/verify assertions; test_unstructured/partition/test_md.py:54-100 cover partition_md url/status/content-type; test_unstructured/partition/test_auto.py:1008-1020 covers request_timeout routing for partition(url=...). The fix adds test_unstructured/test_safe_http.py (fix.diff:173-672). HTTP is mocked in all of these, so they run offline.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a hostname/IP-literal denylist check on the url string in the branch the report shows (partition_html's url= path), or wrap requests.get in a one-line URL check, leaving the other two call sites and the DNS-resolved/redirect-hop addresses unvalidated.

out_of_scope_notes: unstructured/partition/api.py:298-325 POSTs local document bytes to a caller-supplied api_url; that is service-endpoint configuration rather than URL-based document fetching, so it is outside this advisory's protection and was only noted.
unstructured/embed/octoai.py:20 takes a configurable base_url for an LLM endpoint (outbound request whose destination the caller sets); outside this advisory, noted only.
unverified: Repo size in MB not measured (no shell available this session); O12 tiny_repo/giant_repo were therefore not asserted (the tree is clearly a large multi-hundred-module Python project).
The published advisory body itself was not available offline; the landing point and the 'URL-based partitioning' framing are inferred from the supplied summary plus the fix diff.

O7: no schema/serializer/cache/mapper/config_loader producer exists for the checked URL at the pinned commit (the url is a plain function argument, recorded into metadata at unstructured/partition/common/metadata.py:247-250 after the fetch), so there is no producer for the check to call.

All user-supplied-URL fetch routes at the pinned commit are unstructured/partition/auto.py:310, unstructured/partition/html/partition.py:161 and unstructured/partition/md.py:97 (grep of requests./urllib/httpx across unstructured/), and the fix changes all three; hence O8 is empty. The remaining network calls use fixed URLs (unstructured/utils.py:199 telemetry, unstructured/nlp/tokenize.py:42 spaCy model download).

The diff's modified tests exist at the pinned commit in their pre-fix form, mocking requests.get (test_unstructured/partition/html/test_partition.py:1276-1277, test_unstructured/partition/test_md.py:64); the diff's new test_unstructured/test_safe_http.py is absent from the pinned tree, so no regression test leaks the expected fix and regression_tests_in_pinned_commit is not raised.
file_and_type_from_url (unstructured/partition/auto.py:303) is directly callable and also reaches the sink; it is counted as a call site rather than a separate public entry point, so O1 is 3.

Test behaviour after a fix was not executed (reading only): in particular whether the existing headers/verify assertions (test_unstructured/partition/html/test_partition.py:120, 246) constrain the shape of an acceptable fix.
